It is the only gradient or highlighted text in the captured page; the other headings and all body text are solid dark brown.

evidence.description: Computed style of the h1: background-image linear-gradient(90deg, rgb(255, 138, 0), rgb(255, 45, 111)), background-clip text, color rgba(0, 0, 0, 0), font-size 72px, font-weight 800.

contextual_exceptions.rationale: The supplied context documents this gradient as a brand-guide requirement for the wordmark and main headline, and it appears once rather than repeating across sections, so VIS-02's repetition rule is not met either. The sunrise colours also fit the festival's name. Also checked under VIS-01: one gradient is excluded there and no palette package recurs across regions.

observation_confidence.reason: Computed style on the captured h1 and the rendered screenshot both show the gradient text.

quality_observations.observation: The gradient headline has low contrast against the light page background. Rendered text runs from about rgb(255, 137, 0) at the left to about rgb(255, 93, 54) at the right end of the letters; against the background sampled from the screenshot, about rgb(255, 250, 243), that is roughly 2.3:1 to 2.9:1, below the WCAG 2.x AA minimum of 3:1 for large text. The headline is still legible in the screenshot.

evidence.description: Computed gradient stops rgb(255, 138, 0) and rgb(255, 45, 111) on the h1, with the text filled by the gradient.

consequence.reason: Text is 72px bold and readable in the capture, but falls below the large-text contrast guideline, which may affect low-vision readers.

summary.text: No accepted findings. The one candidate cue, the orange-to-pink gradient on the main headline and wordmark, is recorded as a contextual exception under VIS-02: the supplied context documents it as a brand-guide requirement, it appears once rather than as a repeated device, and its sunrise colours fit the festival's name. The rest of the captured page is plain and specific: named acts for each of three days that agree with the stated June dates, a named venue and station, a gate time, and prices, with no cards, icons, eyebrow labels, statistic tiles, stock section sequence, or configured animation. Separately, quality notes concern the headline only: its gradient colours fall below the 3:1 large-text contrast guideline against the light background, and the gradient spans the full heading width so its pink end never reaches the letters. These are quality observations, not slop claims. Coverage is one desktop screenshot at scroll 0 with DOM text and computed styles; mobile layout, interactions, and source were not available.
major_limitations: One desktop screenshot at scroll offset 0; no mobile viewport, and content below the first viewport, if any, was not captured (the screenshot shows blank space below the visitor details).
No recorded interactions or source excerpts, so INT-01, INT-02, and SRC-01 are unassessed.
Motion judged only from captured computed styles (animation-name none); transition durations and playback were not recorded.
Contrast ratios use a background colour sampled from screenshot pixels because the page body's computed style was not captured.
The brand requirement comes from the supplied capture-plan context (a synthetic fixture), not from an inspected brand guide.
